reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode through the November 2 close, data fresh: SPX 7,541.40 is 3.86% below its 120-day high, 1.99% below its 50-day but still 3.13% above its 200-day; SMH at $508.31 sits between zones after a 24.34% drawdown, NVDA at $202.06 occupies Zone 1, VIX is 21.15 at its 5-day high, HY OAS is 3.44% and calm, and the mechanical capitulation tally is 2 of 4 with no volume climax and no VIX rollover.
reaction.invalidation: A close above SPX 7,820 with SMH reclaiming its 50-day average ($571.57) and VIX rolling over would prove the correction over and void the Watch stance; conversely HY OAS above 4% would prove it was never just a correction. Either print voids this ladder.

ladder.response: Arm Tranche A prep: 25% deployment only if the capitulation tally reaches 3 of 4 (volume climax or VIX rollover joining zone occupancy and credit calm); otherwise hold bills and wait for the tally.
ladder.trigger: SMH closes into Zone 2 ($470-505) or NVDA closes into Zone 2 ($175-185)

ladder.response: Treat as the trap case: no chasing, no new entries; hold cash and wait for the retest verdict — a failed first bounce is the expected path, not a buying opportunity.
ladder.trigger: SPX bounces into the 7,750-7,820 failure zone (SMH $580-600) without a VIX rollover or credit confirmation

ladder.response: Stand down: the correction becomes a crack or a trend break, the ladder below is void, and the thesis is reassessed from scratch before any deployment.
ladder.trigger: HY OAS rises above 4% or SPX closes below its 200-day average (7,312.74)

ladder.response: Probe tier-A conviction names (AVGO, DDOG) at no more than 20% of intended weight; add only on confirmation, never on the first bounce.
ladder.trigger: Second low holds above the first low with VIX rolling over from 21.15 and an SMH volume climax reversal

reaction.trapRisk: The pivot-and-fail scenario is the base risk this week: a midterm- or earnings-driven bounce into SPX 7,750-7,820 / SMH 580-600 is likely to fail on first attempt, and NVDA sitting in Zone 1 alone is not a buy signal. Entries wait for the second low to hold plus a VIX rollover; chasing the first bounce converts a Watch stance into a trapped long.

strategyPosture: Watch. The correction is real but unconfirmed as a bottom: NVDA sits in Zone 1 and AVGO/DDOG carry tier-A conviction scores, yet no volume climax or VIX rollover has printed, so this is setup, not entry. New money stays in bills until Zone 2 prints or a confirmed second low.

themes.counterRead: Rotation is the base case only while credit stays calm. The divergence itself is real and worth tracking: if lending standards or HY OAS flip, the same price action re-reads as a rollover. Do not buy the dip on index calm alone — the leadership that drove the index is the part that is breaking.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 names average 16.6% below their 52-week highs versus SPX 3.8% below its high — a 12.8-point divergence gap, with GOOGL the weakest at -31.7% and AAPL the strongest at -3.8%. Bank lending standards are LOOSE at 1.7% on SLOOS, far below the ~40% stress threshold, and HY OAS is 3.44% with credit marked calm, not cracking. The damage is concentrated in the handful of names that dominate the index by weight, not in the broad market or the credit channel.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover — Mag7 unwinds while the index holds
themes.narrative: The tape reads as a broad market break: QQQ is down 8.7% in a month and the AI complex is deep in the red, which the news frames as a rollover. The index disagrees — SPX is only 3.86% off its 120-day high at 7,541.40.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS crossing 4% or SLOOS tightening toward stress levels would void the rotation read.

themes.counterRead: Cheap on growth is not a floor. RSI readings in the low 30s across the chain (NVDA 33.3, AVGO 39.3, LRCX 30.7) say oversold, not bottomed — no volume climax reversal has printed and VIX is still at its 5-day high. The setup is real, but the entry trigger has not fired; buying the first bounce is the trap case.
themes.dataAnchor: Revenue is still growing through the drawdown: NVDA +61.4% YoY at $202.06 (-17% from high, RSI 33.3), AVGO +55% YoY with 67.8% gross margin and $26,914M free cash flow (42.1% margin) at $322.23 (-34.9% from high, conviction score 82, tier A), LRCX +131.3% YoY at $227.56 (-48.1% from high, RSI 30.7), DDOG +27.7% YoY with 80% gross margin at $216.10 (-28.1%, score 81), ANET +28.6% YoY at $164.14 (-24.5%, score 77). Thirty-four dislocations are flagged, most of them sentiment-driven rather than thesis-breaking, and AVGO is the single conviction promotion this run.
themes.label: AI infrastructure: fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: The market is pricing AI infrastructure as a busted trade: SMH is down 24.34% from its high and 19.81% in 20 days, NVDA is down 11.81% in a month, and the whole semiconductor chain sits 25-50% below 52-week highs.
themes.watchFor: SMH volume climax with intraday reversal plus VIX rolling over from 21.15 would confirm a tradeable low in the complex.

themes.counterRead: VST insider buying at the trough is the only hard evidence against the unwind, and it is a watch signal, not a buy signal — revenue is deteriorating. The theme needs a demand print (contracted power, not announcements) before the narrative earns its old multiple back.
themes.dataAnchor: The unwind is broad across the theme, not one name: SMR -30.06% (today -3.56%), OKLO -33.65% (today -5.74%), GEV -10.99% in a month, VST -31.6% from its 52-week high at $134.61 with revenue flagged DETERIORATING. The one offsetting data point is insider behavior — VST insiders bought $1.17M at the trough, which is why VST scores 78 as a watchlist promotion rather than a write-off. NXT is the counter-example inside the theme: +10.02% in a month and +16.92% today.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI power: the narrative ran ahead of the data
themes.narrative: Nuclear and AI-power names were priced as the next leg of the AI buildout. That leg is unwinding fastest: SMR -30.06% and OKLO -33.65% in a month, URA -16.29%, CCJ -13.13%.
themes.watchFor: A VST revenue inflection back to recovery, or a new contracted-power print, would re-open the theme; further 1-month declines past -40% without one confirm the unwind.

themes.counterRead: Bonds are not rescuing equities here: the 10-year near 5% with a Fed signaling higher rates means the correction has no rate-cut put. The guardrail is credit, not rates — if HY OAS breaks 4%, the episode stops being a correction and becomes a crack, and the whole ladder below is void.
themes.dataAnchor: Money is tight but credit is not cracking: DFF 3.88%, DGS2 4.56%, DGS10 4.94%, DGS30 5.31%, real 10-year 2.65%, HY OAS 3.44% and explicitly marked calm. VIX is 21.15, up 36.28% in 20 days and at its 5-day high, but that is a fear print without a credit event behind it — the mechanical tally confirms credit-calm as one of its two confirmed signals.
themes.label: Rates and credit: tight money, calm credit — the correction's guardrail
themes.narrative: The Fed is signaling higher rates — the October 27-28 FOMC is still the active high-signal event and the December 8-9 meeting is already anticipated — and the 10-year sits at 4.94% with the 2s10s curve at +0.38.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS above 4% or a December FOMC surprise would break the calm-credit guardrail.

themes.counterRead: Event-week volatility cuts both ways: a clean AMD print or a midterm result the market reads as gridlock could fuel the bounce into the failure zone — the trap case. Do not let one good print reclassify a correction that has not confirmed a low.
themes.dataAnchor: The earnings reaction is already visible in the tape: PLTR is down 9.39% today and 11.62% in a month after reporting, and GOOGL sits at $278.99 (-31.7% from high, RSI 21.2, the most oversold large name in the input) after its own print. The week's headline set is dominated by the same names — AAPL, PLTR, AMD, SMCI, SHOP — plus jobs and the midterms. The only high-materiality single-name news item is a stale TMDX earnings miss from May 6, which carries no fresh signal.
themes.label: Event week: midterms today, earnings tonight, jobs Friday
themes.narrative: The week is stacked with binary events — US midterm elections today (13 news hits, medium signal), AMD earnings after the close tonight, and the October jobs report Friday November 6 — and the market is pricing that uncertainty with VIX up 38.53% in a month.
themes.watchFor: AMD's print tonight and the October jobs report Friday November 6; either can set the week's direction, neither confirms a bottom on its own.

watchFor: QQQ close versus ~$684 — holding it keeps the Labs sell line untriggered; losing it confirms the QQQ breakdown
SMH close into Zone 2 ($470-505) versus reclaim of the Zone 1 floor ($540)
VIX rolling over from its 21.15 five-day high, versus a spike above 25
HY OAS crossing 4% — the line between correction and credit crack
SPX close below its 200-day average (7,312.74) versus reclaim of the 7,750-7,820 failure zone
whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds in semiconductors: SMH at $508.31 is 24.34% off its high and 2.26% below its 200-day, sitting between Zone 1 ($540-565) and Zone 2 ($470-505). The trigger is either a close into Zone 2, which arms Tranche A, or a failed bounce into the SMH $580-600 failure zone, which confirms the trap.
